rules.text: Main is the global reference view over one physical set of user files; named views are subset projections, never content stores. .rotli/main.json and version-1 views.json hold portable reference trees. Named-view writes synchronize singular Markdown view_tag metadata while boards/binaries stay frontmatter-free. The memex remains durable truth; do not add a content database.

Dependencies point domain -> application -> adapters -> composition -> presentation. Vendor libraries and Tauri stay behind narrow adapters; a dependency swap should normally change one adapter, focused tests, and a composition root.

Repository contracts live in docs/ and code. CARL is compact recall, not a second specification. AGENTS.md owns AI process rules; docs/README.md routes deeper reading. Update the owning contract and CHANGELOG.md when applicable.

docs/development/adding-things.md is the placement authority for new code: surfaces/dialogs in src/components (feature-owned exceptions enumerated), clean-feature split or a named check-architecture exemption, vendors behind allowlisted adapters, pure utilities in src/lib vs effectful src/services, and TS-Rust shared values through scripts/fixtures/parity.json asserted by both parity suites. New tool caches ship their .gitignore entries in the same change.

Every bug fix starts with a failing reproduction. Features cover success, refusal/failure, and meaningful boundaries. AI behavior adds deterministic offline evals; cross-surface gestures add E2E when unit tests cannot prove wiring. bun run check includes TypeScript, oxfmt, oxlint, mechanical guards, all Bun tests, named evals, and runtime/design regressions. bun run verify is CI's local twin (check + build + site/, e2e, clippy + cargo test) and the completion gate; bun run check alone is not.

SYNTAX.md owns naming and style: src TypeScript files/folders are camelCase; scripts, e2e, docs, and breve-runtime use kebab-case; Rust modules use snake_case. TypeScript identifiers follow camelCase/PascalCase roles, CSS uses kebab-case semantic-token classes, and IPC commands are multi-segment snake_case. Mechanical checks own exceptions.

Claude, Codex, scripts, and humans use the packaged rotli JSON CLI or rotli-workspace stdio MCP over one Rust workspace service. Note reads are text/markdown editor bodies without managed frontmatter and include metrics. Secure/secret-shaped notes are omitted; secure/locked writes are refused; every body write needs a fresh revision. New notes enter wiki/_inbox and Main; optional named-view creation/assignment keeps Main global and synchronizes view_tag. agent doctor is read-only; agent self-test uses a temporary memex.

Durable files and public CLI/MCP surfaces evolve additively or through an explicit versioned migration. Preserve unknown user data, make migrations idempotent and atomic, test downgrade behavior, and open unsupported newer writable contracts read-only rather than stamping them down.

Use an ADR only for a cross-boundary decision that is expensive to reverse or easy to re-litigate. Current contracts own normative rules; code/tests prove behavior; CARL stores only a compact accepted-decision summary linked to the ADR.

Review findings become mechanical guards: when Greptile or any reviewer flags a CLASS of issue (not a one-off), the same PR lands a guard for that class — a check script assertion, oxlint restriction, parity fixture, or the tracked .githooks/pre-commit (staged-file oxfmt + conflict markers; enable with git config core.hooksPath .githooks). Precedents: check:security's tool local-vs-egress classification, check:ipc, the hook's formatting guard.

The shell runtime is Tauri; Electron is rejected (decision 2026-08-06, docs/design/shell-runtime-decision.md). rotli must stay a good citizen while idle: a hidden window never composites. lib/idleMotion.ts stamps data-idle from the Page Visibility API and one :root[data-idle="hidden"] rule in base.css pauses every animation; check:design-system enforces both the rule's presence and that no stylesheet sets animation-play-state:running. New always-on animations and unguarded intervals are the regression this prevents — WKWebView, unlike Chromium, does not throttle an occluded webview.

decisions.decision: Code-facing architecture, development, brand, and runtime documentation lives in the repository.
decisions.rationale: One versioned home prevents code/document drift. The memex retains broader product knowledge and model-readable protocols.

rules.text: Interactive lane writes chats/ and ALL of wiki/ (2026-08-03 — a filed note stays editable); never identity/personality/history/MAP.md/control files. Filer lane still owns AI metadata keys exclusively. TS and Rust enforce independently.

Secure and locked are independent. SECURE = visibility vs remote: frontier models never receive secure titles, snippets, bodies, or hits, under any setting; on-device models read them BY DEFAULT, withdrawable per note (local_ai_allowed tri-state) or per vault (secureLocalAi). LOCKED = editing: no AI of any class edits a locked note; every class still reads it. The organizer still skips both. Brain memory lanes (identity/, personality/, history/, MAP.md, inbox.md) are Surface::Reference — AI-retrievable, never in the Notes tree, never writable; vault plumbing stays Hidden.

Unknown frontmatter survives byte-for-byte. Rotli owns provenance, the user owns explicit organization/security controls, and the Brain filer owns only declared enrichment fields. Boards and binaries never receive Markdown frontmatter.

Rust APPLIES the filter, not just the verdict: AI retrieval goes through corpus_search_ai / corpus_notes_ai, and every seam putting caller text on a network calls secret::blocked_for_remote (markers + the walk-fed secure-prose ledger), declared in egress-allowlist.json gatedEgressSites.

decisions.decision: User-owned files are durable truth; .rotli/ state must be deletable and rebuildable.
decisions.rationale: Local-first ownership avoids lock-in and keeps files usable without Rotli.

decisions.decision: The Brain organizer defaults to Organize while remaining metadata/location-only, journaled, undoable, and blocked from secure or locked notes.
decisions.rationale: Automatic organization is useful because it never rewrites note prose and every action remains reviewable.

rules.text: Model Mapping 0 builds a fresh capability-sized table of contents per request. Compact models drill in from area maps; larger models receive more direct ids when budgets allow. Pinned and recent items are inspectable priority signals.

Every persisted chat owns one linked background Markdown note with an idempotent managed summary block. Retrieval searches notes and chat transcripts, returns provenance and stable ids, then reads only selected sources before generation.

Retrieval is local-first full text plus metadata and query refinement; no vector database is required. Embeddings may only be an optional rebuildable adapter. Secure content is excluded before mapping, search, read, and provider egress.

Markdown alone owns slash commands, wikilinks, and typed embed fences. DOCX files remain conventional documents; sheets and boards use their native editor boundaries. Inline expansion keeps the parent Markdown tab active unless the user explicitly opens a new tab.

Rotli-created documents and sheets use the managed storage lane; boards remain raw .excalidraw files. Format registries and application workflows are dependency-free, while JSZip, Univer, ExcelJS, and canvas engines stay behind adapters.

DOCX files are locally editable through a framework-free document model, a replaceable Univer adapter, and a Rotli-owned OOXML codec. Saves preserve unrelated package parts and opaque body nodes, create a one-time backup, and never mount Markdown slash or embed capabilities inside the document editor.

Rotli is a workspace, not a preview catalog. Images and video are the only preview-only surfaces. Every other format advertised as supported must provide native editing and saving; otherwise it remains unsupported and must offer an explicit local conversion/import workflow instead of a passive preview.

The Markdown editor is a CodeMirror 6 inline WYSIWYG in src/editor/: livePreview hides syntax and reveals it at the caret; blockRender, tableRender, and fences own widget rendering; the slash menu, wikilinks, and typed embed fences are Markdown-only capabilities. editorSurface.tsx is the pane surface — an enumerated exception to the src/components surface home.

src/editor/model.ts is the live shared text buffer (a state store), not a clean-feature domain model; src/editor sits on check-architecture's named exemption list. New editor capabilities join the existing seams (commands.ts actions, slashActions.ts, embed hosts) rather than introducing a model/ports/workflow split. Placement law: docs/development/adding-things.md.

Mermaid fences remain Markdown source truth and open a View-Visual-Code workspace. Visual mode losslessly edits the supported flowchart subset (shapes, labels, direction, connections, and node colors) while editor positions remain temporary and unsupported syntax fails closed. src/boards/engine/mermaid.ts is a secondary, confirmed conversion into an independent Excalidraw copy; it never claims to round-trip board geometry into Mermaid text.

Wikilink targets normalize before resolution: |display, #heading, and trailing .md strip; path-style targets fall back to their last segment; archived notes resolve (only Trash reads as deleted). An unresolvable wikilink renders dimmed-dashed 'missing' — never a silent dead click. Bare http(s) URLs autolink and open on ⌘-click like [text](url); plain click stays the caret.

Every user-invocable action registers in src/keys/actions.ts so the palette and Settings -> Hotkeys can list and rebind all of it. One dispatcher per webview and no ad-hoc keydown listeners anywhere else; both webviews register the full set while the dispatcher fires only its own surface's actions.

Every command is user-remappable: src/keys/bindings.ts persists user keymaps, chords.ts parses chord sequences, useHeldModifier.ts powers hold-modifier discoverability, and whichKey.tsx renders the key HUD (an overlay, not a dialog — see docs/development/adding-things.md). New shortcuts go through the registry, never raw listeners.

Breve is fully integrated into Rotli. Rotli owns its UI, versioned runtime, configuration surfaces, lifecycle, and scheduler integration. Runtime code is versioned under breve-runtime/; mutable private state remains under .rotli/breve/.

Development must not start the scheduler or write production configuration. Dev may display authorized read-only delivery/watchlist snapshots; dev saves remain temporary. Resend credentials stay write-only in Keychain.

Rotli ships seven theme families — Rotli (warm), Paper & Charcoal (mono), Ocean, Grove, Iris, Blossom, and Midnight — each with an intentionally tuned light and dark environment (fourteen data-theme values; check:design-system asserts every label). Rotli Light is the default and the environment every first run opens in; Paper and Charcoal are the calm mono pair. All surfaces use shared semantic color, type, spacing, focus, and state roles.

Preserve the quiet native-desktop language: readable text, clear hierarchy, semantic surfaces/borders, keyboard safety, and complete states. Product CSS never uses glows, halos, shadows, backdrop blur, decorative filters, fixed --rotli-* palette values, or raw colors; check:design-system enforces the boundary.

A window that is put away must not composite: base.css pauses every animation under :root[data-idle="hidden"], stamped by lib/idleMotion.ts from the Page Visibility API. check:design-system asserts the rule exists and that no stylesheet sets animation-play-state:running, but nothing stops a NEW always-on `animation: … infinite` — prefer state-conditional animation, and guard any interval with document.hidden. WKWebView, unlike Chromium, does not throttle an occluded webview.

decisions.decision: Keep four solid environments—Warm Light, Warm Dark, Paper, and Charcoal—and remove Liquid Glass.
decisions.rationale: Multiple temperatures serve real preferences; Glass added complexity without strengthening the native desktop experience.

rules.text: The memex stores model-readable protocols, prompts, metadata, and capability maps; it never executes provider calls. Rotli owns provider clients, model routing, retrieval execution, and agent orchestration behind application ports.

Model access is capability- and policy-based. Authenticated Breve models may remain available when hidden from the general chat picker, while intentionally blocked individual models stay blocked. Localhost transport does not make a frontier model local.

Model CLASS decides data access, and class is derived from the endpoint plus the provider registry — never an asserted flag. An on-device model (loopback + mlx/llamacpp/ollama) may see secure notes; a frontier model never may, localhost proxy or not. Class buys VISIBILITY only: no class edits a locked note, and every AI write rides corpus_write_ai (read gate, then locked refusal). Headless workspace agents count as remote for content policy even when their process is local.

The canonical threat model owns assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse cases, out-of-scope assumptions, residual risk, and review triggers. Adding an account, telemetry, crash upload, sync, destination, writable surface, credential, or broader capability requires updating it before implementation.

Secure notes are an AI-egress and organizer-access classification, not an encrypted vault. They remain plain local files; macOS account isolation and FileVault provide at-rest protection. Do not place secrets on agent-managed boards because board scenes have no secure classification.

docs/development/security.md owns the executable egress inventory, destination guards, security check procedure, current dependency findings, and dated risk exceptions. New network paths update its allowlist and adversarial fixtures in the same change.

Source edits do not authorize operational mutation. Starting or stopping persistent processes, touching live data or Keychain, installing an app, committing, pushing, deploying, or releasing requires explicit scope and authorization.

Completion validation is bun run check, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml, the production build, and focused tests. Native visual or scheduler claims require human-managed app evidence; browser fixtures are not equivalent.

A production release must trace to a clean reviewed commit with exact-commit CI evidence, matching versions/tags, signed and notarized artifacts, checksums, SBOM/provenance, visible publication failures, key-custody records, and a tested superseding-release or rollback path.

Support diagnostics are local, user-directed, content-free by default, and never automatically uploaded. Reports omit note content/titles/paths, Keychain values, credentials, full memexes, and raw logs; future bundles require an allowlist, secret scan, path normalization, preview, and explicit export.

Substantive code changes land through a feature branch + pull request reviewed by the Greptile GitHub app; findings are fixed and answered on-thread before a squash merge. Releases gate on the merged commit's CI conclusion VALUE, never exit codes. E2E specs drive UI through real controls, never ⌘-chords (Linux CI has no Meta key). Doc-only corrections may commit directly.

The System browser (Library/Assets/Archive/Trash) is a spatial Finder with four views — Icons (image thumbnails), List, Columns, Gallery (big preview + filmstrip, arrow keys) — switched by Finder icons. The folder trail is a BOTTOM path bar whose leaf is the selection; background right-click offers New folder + Sort by (name/kind/modified/created). Listings read disk paths through rerootDiskPath (memex lanes are lowercase on disk); the Library lists wiki notes AND the files/boards inside wiki folders.

The sidebar: one-row header, then a two-segment FRONT switcher — Home (All notes · Captures · Tasks · Main tree) and Chat (New chat · All chats · folders · every chat, uncapped). The active front owns the whole scrolling body. Breve is a MODE replacing the switcher. Home holds the collapsible SYSTEM zone (sec:system, default open); the Files · Librarian · Settings footer shows under every front. Persisted: sidebarView + expandedDests['sec:system']. Chords ⌃1 Home / ⌃2 Chat / ⌃⇧2 New chat / ⌃` toggles front; reveals switch fronts first. Parts live in src/components/sidebar/.

Every tab is closeable including the last: the lone pane goes EMPTY (activeTabOf returns null) and rests on the quokka empty state with new-note/search/reopen actions; ⌘⌥T restores (⌘⇧T is New board). The ⌘K palette follows real pointer movement only (onMouseMove, never onMouseEnter — scroll-under-cursor hover events snap the selection back).

A pane is a BOX: .pane-body clips, so no surface paints into the pane next door — a surface that cannot fit compresses its chrome then scrolls inside its own box, and popovers needing the window are portaled + fixed. Pane sizing has ONE law, clampSplitSizes(sizes, minFrac) over MIN_PANE_WIDTH 320 / chrome-derived MIN_PANE_HEIGHT 220, applied at split time, during a divider drag, and live via a ResizeObserver per split. Dividers carry aria-label, never title.

staging.rule_text: The agent surface is four-tool uniform: AGENTS.md is canonical for Claude (@AGENTS.md import in CLAUDE.md), Codex and Cursor (native root read), and Antigravity (.agents/rules/AGENTS.md symlink, byte-equality gated). All four reach the same project CARL MCP server; Cursor and Antigravity launch it with CARL_READONLY=1, which hides and refuses carl_stage_proposal — only Claude or a human stages proposals. Repo skills live canonically in .agents/skills (SKILL.md standard); .claude/skills symlinks there. check:docs asserts wiring, mirror integrity, skills parity, and read-only behavior.
staging.rationale: 2026-08-19 four-tool parity work: Cursor and Antigravity previously had no repo wiring at all, and the read-only boundary existed only for Codex (config-level). Now the server enforces it and the gate smoke-tests it.

staging.rule_text: Rotli Web requires a connected vault folder and never stores notes in the browser. Its /app/ CSP reaches only http://127.0.0.1 (check:web-privacy + e2e/web/rotli-web-privacy.spec.ts). Rotli Helper may serve ONE vault a person chose (--vault or the OS picker, never the page): paths via resolve_beneath, symlinks skipped, .git never written, revision-gated atomic writes, vault verbs only from the vault adapter (never the AI seam). A lost connection is a reconnect screen, never a stand-in vault.
staging.rationale: 2026-09-22 the owner reversed the helper's 'no vault access' threat model so Zen/Firefox write real files, required a vault on the web, and made privacy (nothing leaves the computer) the top rule. Contract: docs/architecture/web-vault-connection.md.
